facts.statement: Volgatitan was first described in November 2018 by Russian paleontologists Alexander Averianov and Vladimir Efimov.
facts.quote: It was first described in November 2018 by Russian palaeontologists Alexander Averianov and Vladimir Efimov.

facts.statement: Volgatitan lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Ulyanovsk Oblast of Russia.
facts.quote: Volgatitan (meaning "Volga giant") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of the Ulyanovsk Oblast, Russia.

facts.statement: The only known species, Volgatitan simbirskiensis, is known from seven caudal vertebrae belonging to a single individual.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Volgatitan simbirskiensis, known from seven caudal vertebrae from a single individual.

facts.statement: Fossils of Volgatitan were found in the Ulyanovsk Oblast in Russia.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en el óblast de Uliánovsk, en Rusia.

facts.statement: Volgatitan simbirskiensis is the only known species, identified from seven tail vertebrae of one animal.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida es , conocida a partir de siete vértebras caudales de un único individuo.

facts.statement: Every vertebra possesses a strong crest on the ventral surface of the body, which is the only known unique trait of this taxon.
facts.quote: Todas las vértebras tienen una fuerte cresta en la superficie ventral del cuerpo, la única autapomorfia conocida del taxón.

facts.statement: The estimated average mass of Volgatitan is 17.3 metric tons.
facts.quote: La estimación de masa promedio para el Volgatitan fue de 17,3 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 1982, Soviet scientist Vladimir Efimov discovered large bones embedded in pyrite nodules near the village of Slate Rudnik in the Ulyanovsk region while searching for fossils along the right bank of the Volga River.
facts.quote: En 1982, el científico soviético Vladimir Efimov, mientras buscaba fósiles en la orilla derecha del Volga, cerca del pueblo de Slate Rudnik en la región de Ulyanovsk, descubrió grandes huesos incrustados en dos nódulos de pirita.

facts.statement: A total of seven fragmentary vertebrae were extracted from the fossil site.
facts.quote: Se extrajeron un total de 7 vértebras fragmentarias.

facts.statement: The genus name Volga honors the river where the fossils were found, while the suffix 'titan' refers to divine beings from Greek mythology.
facts.quote: El nombre del género, Volga, se colocó en honor al río a orillas del cual se encontraron los fósiles, con la adición de la palabra "titan", que en la mitología griega significa seres divinos de la segunda generación que precedieron a los olímpicos.

facts.statement: The specific name simbirskiensis honors Simbirsk, the former name of the city Ulyanovsk.
facts.quote: El nombre específico se da en honor a Simbirsk, el antiguo nombre de Ulyanovsk.

facts.statement: Volgatitan lived between 136 and 130 million years ago, spanning the Hauterivian to Barremian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: vivió a principios del período Cretácico, entre 136 a 130 millones de años desde el Hauteriviense al Barremiense

facts.statement: Volgatitan is the oldest known titanosaur from the Northern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: Es el más antiguo titanosaurio conocido del hemisferio norte

facts.statement: While initially classified as a titanosaur related to Lognkosauria, later studies suggest Volgatitan may belong to the family Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: It was initially described as a titanosaur related to Lognkosauria, but a later study suggests it may instead be a member of Mamenchisauridae.

facts.statement: A 2026 phylogenetic analysis by Mannion and Carvalho placed Volgatitan within the family Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: In 2026, Mannion and Carvalho included Volgatitan in their phylogenetic analysis, and found it to be a member of the family Mamenchisauridae.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Averianov and Efimov identified Volgatitan as a member of the clade Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético de los autores , centrado en los titanosáuridos con la adición del Tengrisaurus descrito en 2017, identificó a Volgatitan como miembro del clado Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Volgatitan is the first European representative and the geologically oldest member of the Lithostrotian lineage, which previously contained only South American species.
facts.quote: Este grupo anteriormente solo contenía representantes sudamericanos. Volgatitan es el primer representante europeo y geológicamente el más antiguo de esta línea.

facts.statement: The discovery suggests the Lithostrotian lineage leading to Lognkosauria had a much wider distribution than previously thought and went extinct everywhere except South America by the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de este dinosaurio sugiere que el linaje Lithostrotia, que conduce al clado Lognkosauria, tenía una distribución mucho más amplia de lo que se pensaba anteriormente, y se extinguió en todas partes excepto en América del Sur a finales del Cretácico.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Volgatitan's parent group as Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mamenchisauridae

facts.statement: Volgatitan lived during the Hauterivian stage, approximately 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)
